title: MOS capacitor: gate charge and low-frequency C-V from accumulation to inversion (analytic)
description:
A 1D MOS stack along y (two 0.5 nm cells wide): p-type silicon substrate (N_A = 1e22 1/m^3, n_i 1e16, 0.8 um, ohmic body contact on the bottom 10 nm at 0 V), 10 nm oxide (eps_dc 3.9, n_intrinsic 0) and a 2 nm gate layer on the oxide (gate feature, mid-gap: work_function_difference 0). The sweep runs over the surface band bending psi_s = -0.1..0.8 V (accumulation, depletion, inversion; 2 phi_F = 0.71 V) and sets the gate voltage from it, so no implicit solve is needed: V_g = V_fb + psi_s + Q_g / C_ox, V_fb = V_bulk = -V_T asinh(N_A / 2 n_i) (gate potentials are referred to the intrinsic level), C_ox = eps0 3.9 / t_ox = 3.45e-3 F/m^2. The model holds two identical drift_diffusion physics on the same stack: mos at V_g and mos_dv at V_g + dV_g (dV_g = 1 mV); their gate charge difference is the low-frequency (equilibrium: the body contact supplies the inversion electrons) capacitance. SRH lifetime 1e-10 s: the equilibrium does not depend on it, but in inversion the electron level of the surface layer is tied to the body only through SRH generation and minority diffusion across the depletion region; with 1e-6 s that tie is so weak that the Newton updates stall at the round-off floor near psi_s = 0.8 V.
Analytic (exact Poisson-Boltzmann first integral): Q_g = sign(psi_s) sqrt(2 eps_s q V_T) sqrt(p0 (e^(-u) + u - 1) + n0 (e^u - u - 1)), u = psi_s / V_T; C_s = dQ_g / dpsi_s = sqrt(2 eps_s q V_T) |p0 (1 - e^(-u)) + n0 (e^u - 1)| / (2 V_T sqrt(...)); C = 1 / (1 / C_ox + 1 / C_s), evaluated at the midpoint surface potential psi_s + (dV_g / 2) C_ox / (C_ox + C_s) of the two gate voltages (second-order accurate).
Derived values tab: Q_gate = mos_charge_gate / Lx against Q_g, Q_space = integral of the space charge / Lx against -Q_g (Gauss), C_lf = (mos_dv_charge_gate - mos_charge_gate) / (dV_g Lx) against C, and C_ratio = C_lf / C_ox. Expect ~1e-3 (discretisation of the 4-8 nm accumulation / inversion layers by 0.5 nm cells; less in depletion).
Sweep tab: the four derived values versus psi_s with their dashed curves (C: C_ox in accumulation, the depletion minimum near 2 phi_F, back toward C_ox in inversion).
Line profile tab (last sweep value, psi_s = 0.8 V): V_oxide, the linear potential across the oxide from V_bulk + psi_s at the interface with slope Q_g / (eps0 3.9). Field tab: V, N, P, space_charge of mos.

parameters.name: psi_s
parameters.description: surface band bending in V, positive toward depletion / inversion (the sweep runs -0.1..0.8 V)

parameters.name: T_lat
parameters.description: lattice temperature in K (the semiconductor temperature setting)

parameters.name: eps_ox
parameters.description: static relative permittivity of the oxide

parameters.name: tau_srh
parameters.description: SRH lifetime of both carriers in s (no effect on the equilibrium; short so the inversion electrons are tied to the body numerically)

parameters.name: dx_cell
parameters.description: uniform cell size (8 cells per 4 nm inversion layer at 0.8 V)

parameters.name: C_ox
parameters.description: oxide capacitance per area in F/m^2 (3.45e-3)

parameters.name: V_bulk
parameters.description: bulk potential -V_T asinh(N_A / 2 n_i) in V (-0.357 V) = flat-band voltage of a mid-gap gate

parameters.name: A_s
parameters.description: prefactor sqrt(2 eps_s q V_T) of the first integral

parameters.name: Q_g
parameters.description: analytic gate charge per area in C/m^2 (= minus the semiconductor charge)

parameters.name: V_g
parameters.description: gate voltage of physics mos in V

parameters.name: dV_g
parameters.description: gate voltage step of physics mos_dv in V

parameters.name: C_s_s
parameters.description: semiconductor capacitance dQ / dpsi at psi_s in F/m^2

parameters.name: psi_mid
parameters.description: surface potential at the mid gate voltage V_g + dV_g / 2 in V

parameters.name: C_s_m
parameters.description: semiconductor capacitance at psi_mid in F/m^2

parameters.name: C_ref
parameters.description: analytic low-frequency capacitance per area in F/m^2
